question.leadin: The Treaty of Luebeck ended the Danish involvement in this conflict.
question.text: Name this conflict that began with the Bohemian Revolt and the Defenestration of Prague and primarily pitted the Hapsburgs and their allies against the Bourbons and their allies.
question.clue: This war's Bohemian phase ended at the Battle of White Mountain, which saw a victory for Count Tilly.

swap.leadin: Also known as Henry Bolingbroke, this man became King of England after deposing Richard II in 1399.
swap.text: Identify this English king who was later succeeded by his son upon his 1413 death.
swap.clue: This ruler, who was assassinated by the zealot Francois Ravaillac, was married to Marie de Medici, who later led the "Day of the Dupes" against Cardinal Richelieu.

question.text: The title Emperor of the Romans would later morph into this position, holders of which were chosen by German Prince-Electors. Other holders of this title included Otto the Great and Frederick Barbarossa.
question.answerHtml: Holy Roman Emperor [accept German-Roman Emperor or Romanorum Imperator or Rex Romanorum; prompt on Emperor; do not accept or prompt on “Roman Emperor”]
question.clue: The Treaty of Pressburg invalidated this office after the battle of Austerlitz in 1806, and it was selected by seven electors after the 1356 Golden Bull.

swap.leadin: This Habsburg ruler, the son of Philip I of Castile, ruled both the Low Countries and Spain during the early to mid-1500s.
swap.text: Name this Holy Roman Emperor, the father of Philip II, who fought against both France and the Ottomans.
swap.answerHtml: Charles V [accept Charles I of Spain; prompt on Charles]
swap.clue: He signed the Peace of Augsburg with the Schmalkaldic League and during the Italian Wars captured Francis I at the Battle of Pavia.

question.leadin: This emperor convened the Diet of Roncaglia after crushing Milan.
question.text: Name this Holy Roman Emperor, who drowned in the Saleph River. He is nicknamed for his red beard.
question.answerHtml: Frederick Barbarossa [accept Frederick I; prompt on Frederick or Barbarossa alone]
question.clue: This man journeyed with Phillip II Augustus after taking up the cross at the Diet of Mainz.

swap.leadin: This group developed special war wagons that provided some of the first mobile artillery in history.
swap.text: Name this group that followed the teachings of a reforming theologian who was burned at the stake after the Council of Constance.
swap.clue: These people, led by Jan Zelivsky, threw Catholic magistrates out of a window during the First Defenestration of Prague.

question.text: The king of this territory served as the third elector. Frederick the Winter King ruled this territory during the 30 Years War, and it was earlier ruled by King Wenceslas.
question.clue: A university in this region's New Town was founded by Charles IV, who was crowned after his blind father John died at the Battle of Crecy.

swap.text: In the less-famous First Defenestration of Prague, seven city council members were killed by followers of this Czech religious reformer, who was condemned to death at the Council of Constance.
swap.clue: Prokop the Great led forces that pioneered the use of war wagons among this man's Taborite followers in a 15th-century conflict.

question.leadin: This man may have helped complete Odo of Metz's designs for a palace in Aachen, and he once dispatched a servant to pilfer holy remains from Rome to increase the piety of churches he founded.
question.text: Identify this colleague of Alcuin, a preeminent Frankish biographer from the eighth and ninth centuries.
question.clue: The preface to this notoriously short man's most famous work was written by Walafrid Strabo.

swap.text: The third Holy Roman Emperor with this name was a close ally of the Piast king Boleslaw I. The first Holy Roman Emperor of this name, nicknamed "the Great," beat the Magyars at Lechfeld in 962.
swap.answerHtml: Otto [or Otto III; or Otto I; or Otto the Great]
swap.clue: The fourth and final one was the only Welf to become emperor, but was defeated at the Battle of Bouvines, after which Frederick II restored the Hohenstaufen Dynasty.

question.text: This confederation of electorates in the Holy Roman Empire fought for Lutheranism against Charles V before being routed at the Battle of Muhlberg.
question.clue: Taking its name from a town in Thuringia, this group was first formed by Philip I of Hesse and John Frederick I of Saxony.

swap.leadin: This battle was part of a consolidation of power that started after Liudolf's rebellion.
swap.text: Name this battle that took place near Augsburg, a victory for the husband of Adelaide and son of Henry the Fowler.
swap.clue: At the onset of this battle, the brother-in-law of the winning commander returned from exile to fight in this conflict.

question.leadin: Its chapel has a famous octagonal dome and its hot sulphur springs made it a popular nineteenth-century spa resort.
question.text: Name this city that was the namesake of treaties ending the War of Devolution and the War of Austrian Succession. It was also the capital of the Carolingian empire of Charlemagne.
question.clue: Ravenna's San Vitale was probably the model for this city's Palatine Chapel.

swap.text: This first king of the Ottonian dynasty gets his nickname from the legend that he was fixing birding nets when told that he had been elected King of Germany.
swap.clue: His wife accompanied him on his campaigns building monasteries, one of which was their burial site of Quedlinburg.

question.text: At Lutzen, Gustavus Adolphus fought this duke of Friedland, a Catholic general recalled by Holy Roman Emperor Ferdinand II. His apparent scheme to ally with Protestants led to his murder in 1634.
question.clue: One of the Catholic leaders at White Mountain was the Count of Tilly, who, along with this man, was one of the key Hapsburg commanders during the Thirty Years War. This man lost the Battle of Lutzen to Gustavus Adolphus and was killed after contemplating defection to the Protestant side.

swap.text: A Danish king of this name ceded Norway to Sweden in order to avoid an occupation of Jutland. A much earlier ruler of the Palatinate with this name was known as the "Winter King."
swap.answerHtml: Frederick [or Frederik; accept Frederick VI or Frederick V or Frederick the Winter King]
swap.clue: Another emperor with this name was defeated by the Lombard League at the Battle of Legnano.

question.text: The pornocracy began to end when John XII crowned this man as the first Holy Roman Emperor but then turned on him, after which this German ruler deposed John and installed Leo VIII.
question.answer: Otto I or Otto the Great
question.clue: This ruler won at Recknitz, and was able to win his most famous battle because his forces remained cohesive despite attacks on his baggage train.

swap.leadin: John of Bohemia, of Crecy fame, originally gave Charles IV this name, but Charles renamed himself in honor of Charles the Fair of France.
swap.text: Give this name of several rulers of Prague, like Charles' Nepomuk-killing son. A beloved duke of this name was murdered by his not-so-good brother, Boleslaus the Cruel.
swap.clue: This name was borne by the protege of Saint Ludmila who was killed after refusing to fight Henry the Fowler.

question.leadin: He spent the first few years of his reign putting down a revolt led by Boleslav of Bohemia and Henry the Wrangler. FTPE.
question.text: Name this emperor, whose brothers included the rebellious Liudolf of Swabia.

swap.text: This Bohemian king, the son of Holy Roman Emperor Henry VII and Margaret of Brabant, died fighting at the Battle of Crecy despite being blind. He shares his royal name with an English ruler called "Lackland."
